answer: Joining must cost sequential time. Each identity produces a verifiable-delay proof of difficulty D = n x D0, seeded by the prior checkpoint hash, unknowable, so proofs cannot be pre-farmed, and the challenge embeds the applicant's key, so proofs never transfer. Witnessing nodes recheck each admission against that seed, rejecting skips like strata in shale. Pricing: D0 is tuned so one identity's wait costs 0.5% of epoch reward R. A dune of fakes pays m x D sequential seconds, and D grows linearly with n, so marginal cost never flattens; the onyx ledger archives all proofs.
